name: Rubrik

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Very Heavy - hard-rated DSA/OOP/distributed-systems problems across 3-6 rounds, with an extremely low pass rate reported for the Bengaluru pipeline (14% across tracked interviews) and coding rounds that can shift into system design mid-question
rounds: Technical screening: a coding round that can include semaphore/mutex (concurrency) questions even at the screening stage

2-3 DSA/competitive-programming rounds: medium-hard problems (2D dynamic programming, tree/LCA, two-pointer, DFS + binary search, priority-based task allocation) implemented on a shared doc or interviewing tool - some rounds combine an online assessment of 4 DSA questions (trees, partitioning, DP, arrays) before the live rounds

System coding round(s): implementing low-level distributed-systems components (e.g. producer-consumer with multithreading, a task scheduler with multithreading) - one report notes the coding round "shifted into system design midstream," rewarding candidates who can extend a solution live
System design round (later-stage): a specific product/service design (e.g. "design Twitter with a notification service")
Hiring-manager round: interests and CV-based discussion
extraTopics: Concurrency and distributed-systems reasoning (mutex/semaphore, multithreading, producer-consumer patterns) tested directly in coding, not as a separate theory round
Staying composed when a "coding" question evolves into a system-design discussion mid-interview - flagged as the single biggest differentiator between candidates who pass and who don’t
Sustained hard-level DSA output across 2-3 back-to-back rounds
Software Engineer.notes: The Bengaluru pipeline specifically is reported as extremely selective: a 14% pass rate across 7 tracked interview experiences, with round count varying from 3 to 6 depending on report.
